answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure on SMB is acute, but memory_73 shows promotional pricing materially damaged 30-day retention despite acquisition lift—a poor fit for sustainable long-term revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well but only on established customers, not on churning price-sensitive accounts. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB crisis. Simplify onboarding (memory_31, exp_31) shows modest gains but is already implemented. Activation messaging (memory_91, exp_91) offers the highest leverage: it improved both engagement and retention without cannibalizing revenue, and its mechanism—nudging accounts to first meaningful action—directly addresses why price-sensitive SMBs churn (low engagement leads to low perceived value). Deploying enhanced in-product activation messaging to price-sensitive SMB cohorts targets engagement lift before price becomes the decisive factor, preserving retention and customer lifetime value. Scale as standard experiment to measure efficacy against SMB churn specifically, then roll to broader base if confirmed.
